questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me a student of Eastern European studies being in Estonia was an opportunity be closer to the "action". The university of Tartu is a university I already was familiar with regarding the quality and its history as an important educational institution in the Baltics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I sadly became unexpectedly sick so that I wasn't able to fully immerse myself in the Erasmus experience as I wanted to, but my fellow students, facilities and the university were great for the short time I got to be there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very hard, especially from Copenhagen. I felt left alone in the process especially with regards to the learning agreement where I had to contact people in the administration almost at random to get help. In the end I got help form my friend who had similar experiences, but managed to get help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a good dialog with the incoming student advisor in Tartu via mail. I got the help that they were able to provide, especially with my pre-arrival questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I came when there still was a somewhat lockdown in Tartu, but they were able to help me.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the student dorms. Options were few for my instance because of the Covid situation.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen in the "apartment" with everything available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can get noisy, but i guess that is a part of the experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy. Most information was available on a website where you could see courses, prerequisite and how many spaces there were. Registration was done by simply clicking on preferred classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All that was needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones that I wanted from the the available classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some courses get filled out fast so do everything early. You can also switch if needed later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good quality of lectures, interesting and it held a high level without being hard to follow.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: What I expected. Somewhat different from Copenhagen where the lecturers had more quizzes and less "independence". Other than that very good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It had less independent learning and attendance was actively followed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Development in the Baltic Sea region. 
It was a good course and because its studying the region it is in you get a good understanding of the subject.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sporting events, social gatherings, Estonian culture days, parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Every culture activities, because Estonia has an unique and interesting culture

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the other Baltic states and the Estonian coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No problems at all.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join as many activities as you can.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many people from many countries, but it was more fun than difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Wanting to help you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Pay attention to the required stuff, school attendance and papers.
Do not spend too much time studying.
Have fun,.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find housing early.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Privacy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
